title: Process: refresh a conflicting PR only at merge time; a clean merge of main keeps its review; only the owner's reviews count

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Asked for by the maintainer, 2026-11-12: "We need to maybe modify the merge-ready skill to be better at analyzing merge-order and batch how the PR's are going in to generate as little delta pr's as possible. we spend a shit ton of tokens on uncessary deltas." and, on the maintenance lane, "Stop the other sessions work as well for now until we can figure out how it stops causing conflicts". Decided in the question dialog the same day: **"Refresh only at merge time"**, and yes to changing the repo's rules to match. Folds in #1207 (decided earlier the same day: "No, only ours count").

## The cost today
Every merge moves `main`. Today's rules have a conflicting PR refreshed at once (`/resolve-conflicts`, contributor mode at each session start; the maintenance lane's easy resolutions), and every merge-of-main sent to a delta review (`/resolve-conflicts check`). Numbers from 2026-11-12: 7 refresh merges pushed by the maintenance lane alone, 5 of them on PRs that had no review yet, three branches carrying `conflicts` two or three times in one day although each had been resolved once; each refresh re-stales a review marker and is undone by the next merge to main.

## The rule
1. **Refresh only at merge time.** A conflicting PR carries `conflicts` and is otherwise left alone - by its author's agents, by maintenance, by reviewers. It takes `git merge origin/main` only when it is the next PR in a merge batch (or when its author is pushing a review fix anyway and chooses to). `/resolve-conflicts` contributor mode stops being a start-of-session duty; it becomes the tool the merging session (or the author, when asked for a specific PR) uses at merge time.
2. **Merge in batches, in a simulated order.** The merging session collects the ready PRs, simulates the merges (`git merge-tree --write-tree`, no checkout or build), merges the largest cleanly-merging sequence first - none of those needs a refresh - and then refreshes the conflicting ones strictly one at a time, each merged before the next is refreshed. A reference implementation lives in the maintainer's local `merge-ready` skill (`scripts/plan_merge_order.py`); bring the planner into the repo (an `xtask` subcommand or a script under `.claude/skills/`) so forks have it.
3. **A clean merge of main keeps its review.** If every commit since the reviewed head is a merge of `main` whose `git show --remerge-diff` is empty, the tree is exactly what merging the reviewed head would give: the review stands, the label is restored without an agent, and no delta review is run. Hand edits confined to rule-settled files (`.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`, `CHANGELOG.md`, snapshot PNGs taken from main, `Cargo.lock`) are read by the merging session itself. Only a conflict resolved by hand gets a delta review, and that review reads the remerge-diff only (rebuild when logic was merged by hand). New commits get a review of those commits.
4. **Only the owner's reviews count** (#1207). A `pr-reviewer` / `review-cost` marker counts only in a comment or review authored by the repository owner's account, and `merge-ready` only when that account set it; a contributor's pre-check is a plain comment without the marker. `/review-prs` step 1, `/resolve-conflicts check`, and the PR-reviewer agent filter on the author; a `merge-ready` set by another account with no owner-authored marker for the current head is removed with a one-line comment.
5. **One gate per batch.** The batch tier runs once on main after a merge batch, not after each merge.

## Files
`AGENTS.md` ("Conflicted PRs are re-merged by their author", "Overlapping issues stack", "Every PR opens as a draft" where it speaks of `git merge origin/main`, "Outside PRs are reviewed", the cut's step 1), `.claude/skills/resolve-conflicts/`, `.claude/skills/review-prs/`, `.claude/agents/PR-reviewer.md`, the planner's new home; `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` bump; announcement on #681 saying what a fork must change (stop start-of-session refreshes; stop marking and labelling own PRs).

Keep every quoted maintainer sentence; where a quoted instruction is superseded, say so with the date, as the claim-liveness law does.

Done means: the five points are in the process text; `/review-prs` lists a PR whose only marker for its head is by another account; `/resolve-conflicts check` restores `merge-ready` on an empty-remerge-diff refresh without dispatching a review and never asks an author to refresh a PR that is not about to merge; the planner runs from the repo on Windows, macOS and Linux with its own unit tests for the ordering logic; PROCESS_VERSION bumped and announced.
